items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: His act was on the style of Morris Rocco, an American Negro who was very popular in the downtown theatre circle of many big cities and white night clubs in the States.

ctx.x: We checked into a hotel and Fred went to find his man in order to know what time we would rehearse the show, He came back a few hours later and told us that there was not going to be any show. That was the 11th of March, and we came back to Rome by bus on the 12th. I never knew exactly what happened. Fred paid the expenses for the trip because he was the one that was doing the business such as it was.

I had a room in a place called Pensione Beccari on the via del Tritone and to cut down on expenses, I shared a two roomed bedroom with a hungarian fellow named Pista. Pista was a refugee, and there were quite a number of them-men and women-staying in this pensione. But the day that Lily returned, I moved to another room in the same place. While at this place, I met a West Indian fellow named Stanley Carter. I had heard of him, but never seen him. Stanley played piano and sang. His act was on the style of Morris…

Duke Ellington was on his first tour of Europe after world war II and it was a delightful pleasure to know that he would be coming to Rome during the time I was there. This was in May and Duke played a theatre for 5 to 6 concerts. It was something for Lily also, because she had never seen or heard of a big band playing jazz. The musicians I knew were Jimmy Hamilton, Sonny Greer, Harry Carney, Ray Nance, Al Killian, Russel Procope, Quinton Jackson, Johnny Hodges, the Duke himself, Don Byas who had been engaged to…
